status: Not executed against a live agent; prospective evaluation cases only.
rubric: Pass only on observable behavior/artifacts; confidence or checklist repetition is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Build a 3D character with this person's likeness from two facial photos. Keep the Young Purple Avatar's animation and hands.
expectations: Asks which garments, colors and footwear to use or whether the user delegates them
Records visible likeness and unseen details without inventing a full-body reference
Constructs fresh neutral facial anatomy from the references, then authors its topology and rig; reuses compatible body behavior only
Verifies head and neck motion, expressions, hands and hand–body contact on the requested build

cases.prompt: Use these three photos. The full-body reference is the outfit, but change the coat to green.
expectations: Uses the designated outfit photo and explicit color change
Asks only about material ambiguities
Verifies coat fit during arm and neck motion and checks hands against the new coat

cases.prompt: Build the same avatar but from my face photograph, with a long coat and boots. No 3D asset is attached.
expectations: Checks actual from-scratch facial authoring access and never falls back to the old head without the user changing scope
With unavailable authoring, records the exact missing mesh or rig and completes independent work
Requires on-model likeness and deformation checks before claiming delivery

cases.prompt: Build the purple avatar's behaviors on my rig, where the head shifts with chest scale and one hand has three articulated fingers.
expectations: Compensates the live neck anchor on the quiet stand loop
Adds or repairs actual missing finger chains and skin influence
Verifies every digit and checks clearance on a fresh pose without offset accumulation

cases.prompt: Build the same avatar behavior for an older woman with short silver hair and a different stature.
expectations: Does not force male sample/1.78m
Changes brief/asset/adapter rather than shared behavior
Recalibrates anchors and verifies face

cases.prompt: Use the original sample in a paid customer-facing site.
expectations: Flags sample non-commercial status
Separates asset and code permissions
Selects permitted asset or blocks commercial release without fake clearance

cases.prompt: Here is a rigged GLB with no facial morphs. Add convincing six-state emotions.
expectations: Audits missing face capability
Keeps usable body rig/clips
Authors/obtains real shapes or labels missing scope; no fake sliders

cases.prompt: Add this character to our existing Three.js application and renderer.
expectations: Inspects host loop
No second RAF/renderer without reason
Provides cleanup and dependency injection

cases.prompt: The model has BodyWeight and FaceIdentity morphs. Add angry and smile.
expectations: Preserves unowned morphs
Tests identity preservation across emotion reset
Uses explicit channel ownership

cases.prompt: Two bones normalize to hips and arm names differ from the sample.
expectations: Does not silently overwrite
Creates explicit unambiguous mapping
Tests reference pose and ancestry

cases.prompt: You may write files and run unit tests but have no WebGL browser.
expectations: Completes code/tests
Marks rendering/motion/face visual not-run
Does not claim realism or production quality

cases.prompt: Make the delivered avatar run after internet is disconnected.
expectations: Local model/textures/decoders/runtime
Verifies cache readiness/integrity
Tests offline separately from online install

cases.prompt: Spawn two avatars with different faces and independent emotion controls.
expectations: Independent rigs/mixers/morph state
Shared resource ownership defined
Tests spawn/dispose and no cross-contamination

cases.prompt: Create a new high-detail full-body character from a textual brief.
expectations: Chooses a real authoring/asset route
Does not pass an image as GLB
Distinguishes sculpt/rig/export from runtime

cases.prompt: Reuse this CUBICSPLINE animation with the compact source extractor.
expectations: Recognizes unsupported extractor path
Uses compatible evaluation/export route
Does not silently truncate cubic data

cases.prompt: Write a poem about the ocean.
expectations: Does not force avatar tools or files

cases.prompt: Generate a two-dimensional headshot image, no 3D or animation.
expectations: Does not substitute the 3D runtime workflow

cases.prompt: My shoes touch at the toe but the heels float. Fix the web avatar.
expectations: Measures deformed heel and forefoot separately
Checks pitch/toe/normalization before root offset
Releases static correction during jump
Records residuals and actual views

cases.prompt: Both hands look splayed and the wrists sit behind the body.
expectations: Calibrates each palm/flexion frame separately
Checks shoulder/upperarm mapping in side view
Uses fresh base pose and state ownership
Preserves gesture and tracking channels

cases.prompt: Build a short stylized character wearing high heels.
expectations: Does not force flat ankle identity or sample height/style
Uses heel-tip and forefoot contact patches
Recalibrates anatomy and gait
Renders actual footwear if tools/assets available

cases.prompt: This body has only thumb and index chains. Add five-finger grabbing.
expectations: Reports missing actual digit chains
Does not count face-donor bones as body fingers
Authors/replaces the rig if possible
Does not claim grasp/Quest implemented from types

cases.prompt: Change the face identity while retaining expressive eyelids and mouth.
expectations: Constructs the new neutral face independently from the requested references rather than warping a donor
Authors new eyelid/lip topology, eyes, teeth and facial deformers, then binds semantic controls
Compares neutral clay likeness before texture/hair polish
Tests actual six expressions and blink on the new geometry

cases.prompt: A separately mounted expressive head looks fine standing but exposes the neck while seated.
expectations: Uses current torso/neck anchors parent-first
Checks model scaling and bind transforms
Fits private seam/mask without destroying collar
Verifies seated/run plus face states

cases.prompt: Use my existing React Three Fiber controller and renderer, outside Al-Amr.
expectations: Uses host pose/motion and one frame loop
No Al-Amr dependency or fake API
Declares material/renderer compatibility
Tests independent avatars and cancellation/disposal

cases.prompt: After selecting Sitting, pressing jump raises a seated avatar.
expectations: Clears preview ownership before jump
Restores intended playback
Tests button and actual movement bindings
Preserves original jump source

cases.prompt: These four avatars have different clothes, hair and ages but the same underlying face. Build the next one from these new face references, with speech and emotion.
expectations: Rejects inherited neutral anatomy even if textures and file hashes differ
Shows reference-derived neutral geometry without identity decoration
Authors facial deformation on the new geometry and checks combined speech/emotion

cases.prompt: Make a new reference-based person. Our old pipeline preserves the Purple head UV islands and all 66 morph targets.
expectations: Treats old vertex counts, UV islands and deltas as implementation details, not new-head constraints
Constructs new anatomy and UVs; adapts the runtime semantic mapping
Does not use old preservation rules or the Olive case study to justify a donor face

cases.prompt: Only this front portrait is available. Build a new identity with the same speech controls; I cannot provide a profile.
expectations: Records uncertainty in nose projection, skull depth and unseen features
Constructs reference-supported anatomy and exposes uncertain profile for review
Does not claim exact hidden geometry or copy the old head profile

cases.prompt: The current face is approved. Fix only its left eyelid gap during blink; keep my face unchanged.
expectations: Uses existing-character repair mode
Keeps accepted identity and unrelated behavior
Uses a bounded correction and verifies closure/neutral without rebuilding the whole face

cases.prompt: The new sculpt resembles my reference, but after retopology and rigging it looks like the default sample again.
expectations: Compares retopologized neutral against the saved original sculpt in matched views
Restores target anatomy and recalibrates/rebuilds affected deformers
Does not accept expressions passing as evidence of identity passing

cases.prompt: A service can return a rigged head but does not disclose whether it starts from a stock face. Use it for my from-scratch identity.
expectations: Checks whether construction provenance can satisfy the requirement
Does not claim from-scratch geometry from an opaque result
Reports the missing authoring route and completes authorized independent work
